explanation.walkthrough: 'A nose for the horses' suggests skill at betting; it is a literal nose that horses would like, a carrot.
explanation.definitionFit: The winter figure built in the garden traditionally has pebble or coal eyes and a carrot nose.

clue.text: Group of stars hepcat recalled elevating shows

indicators.note: a thing shown is on display within the words, so the letters are a run inside them
in a down entry, elevating lifts the letters so they read from the bottom

blocks.note: the run straddles the two words, from the end of the first into the second

explanation.surface: A cool jazz fan remembers uplifting performances by a band of stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of stars' sounds like a celebrity band, which a hepcat, a 1940s jazz fan, would recall; it is a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerta, the Lizard, is a small northern constellation, so a named pattern of stars in the sky.

clue.text: Continent as hypothetical person drinking unlimited kir

indicators.note: without limits means without its boundary letters, so only the centre is taken
what is drunk goes inside the drinker, so one piece is put inside the others

blocks.note: taken as written
as in 'person A pays person B'
its middle letter

explanation.surface: A Continental drinker described in the abstract, sipping kir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' seems a link word, but it supplies two letters; the one-letter person then joins it, and the pair enclose the drink. Kir is a French aperitif of white wine and blackcurrant liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest of the world's major landmasses, stretching from the Urals to the Pacific.

clue.text: Squad crossing lake as fire not yet started?

definitions.note: describes such a fire rather than naming it

indicators.note: a piece crossing another passes into it, so one sits inside the other

blocks.note: a unit is a squad
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A fire crew crosses a lake to reach a blaze that has not yet broken out.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition describes a fire's state rather than giving a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlit means not yet set alight, which is the condition of a bonfire before anyone has kindled it.

clue.text: WI must expand part in Jerusalem, say, collectively

blocks.clueFragment: WI must expand part in Jerusalem, say
blocks.note: surface reading: the Women's Institute must enlarge its role in staging a hymn
setter's reading: the members sing their hymn as a single choir, all together

explanation.surface: The Women's Institute has to beef up its contribution to singing Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute, a British women's organisation, famously opens meetings by singing the hymn Jerusalem. 'Part' is a vocal line, and the members sing it in unison.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking or singing in unison means everyone expresses the same thing together, unanimously.

clue.text: Seasonal workers personalities initially ignored

indicators.note: ignoring what comes initially means skipping the opening letter

blocks.note: your selves are your personalities or identities

explanation.surface: Temporary Christmas staff whose characters are overlooked from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seasonal workers' sounds like fruit pickers or shop temps; here the season is Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christmas lore Santa's elves make the toys at the North Pole, working flat out each December.

clue.text: Popular revolutionary Henry is lit up? I deny everything!

indicators.note: a revolution turns things right round, so the letters face the other way
stirred up or mixed up, so the preceding letters are jumbled

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A popular revolutionary called Henry, drunk, protests his innocence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lit up' reads as drunk, but 'lit' is fodder and 'up' alone stirs it. 'I deny everything!' is the definition, voiced by the person.
explanation.definitionFit: A nihilist rejects all moral and religious principles, believing life is meaningless, so they reject every belief.

clue.text: Bravery of woman with honour saving lives

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe within, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: her refers to a woman
the OM, Order of Merit, is a British honour
'lives' as in exists, as in 'he is'

explanation.surface: A decorated woman's courage in rescuing people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving lives' looks like the brave deed itself, but 'saving' holds and 'lives' means exists. The Order of Merit is a British honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroism is great courage, especially in the face of danger, the quality shown by a brave person.

clue.text: This promotes erection of fancy vicarage, not church

indicators.note: 'not' means without, so these letters are taken out
something fancy is elaborately reworked, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
CE, Church of England, is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Planning permission promoting the building of a grand vicarage without a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erection' reads as construction, which suits the vicarage; it is the other kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The drug sildenafil, sold under this brand name, treats impotence by helping men achieve and maintain an erection.

clue.text: Discourage lectures screening single slides

indicators.note: a screen shelters something behind it, so one piece is kept between the others

blocks.note: to deter is to discourage
orates means gives speeches
I is one, a single

explanation.surface: Talks showing just one slide put the audience off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slides' reads as projector slides in a lecture; it is the verb, to decline.
explanation.definitionFit: When standards slide they gradually get worse, which is the same as declining or worsening.

clue.text: Really out of line lawyers unmanned boozer

indicators.note: something taken out of another is removed from it

blocks.note: honestly can mean really, as an intensifier
L is the abbreviation for line
the Bar is the collective name for barristers

explanation.surface: Lawyers' really outrageous behaviour leaves a pub with no staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of line' looks like misbehaving lawyers; it removes the line letter. A boozer is British slang for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An honesty bar is a self-service drinks point, as in a hotel lounge, where guests record their own drinks.
